title: Roe-trace pairing for Inner-Product realizes coarse depth κ ≥ log(R) and certifies a quadratic-log gap against random f
field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW) — coarse geometry / Roe-algebraic K-theory applied to circuit complexity (mathematical branch: noncommutative geometry & geometric group theory)
field_B: Boolean formula depth (NC^1 vs. P): explicit super-logarithmic depth lower bounds via index pairings on the KW-metric space
statement: Let f = IP_n : {0,1}^{2n} → {0,1} be the inner-product-mod-2 function and let (X_f, d_f) be its KW-metric space with d_f(x,y) := log_2(min number of coordinates needed to distinguish x,y). Let c_IP ∈ HX^1(X_f) be the coarse cocycle obtained from the canonical 'parity-of-disagreement' 1-cochain c_IP(x,y) = ⟨x⊕y, x'⊕y'⟩ mod 2 (lifted to Z via signed indicator), and for each propagation parameter R ≥ 1 let T_R ∈ C_u^*[X_f] be the banded Roe operator T_R(x,y) := 1[d_f(x,y) ≤ R]/(1+|B_R(x)|). Then (i) (axiom A5 instance) the trace pairing satisfies log|⟨c_IP, T_R⟩| / log R → α ≥ 1 as n → ∞ and R = o(n), so κ(IP_n) ≥ 1 with this normalization; (ii) (axiom A3 instance) for a uniformly random f' on the same X_{f'} the same construction yields log|⟨c_IP, T_R⟩|/log R → 0 in probability, separating structured and random f.
rationale: This is a direct empirical probe of axioms A5 (Roe-index rigidity: explicit candidates realize a nontrivial pairing whose growth rate is the coarse depth κ) and A3 (anti-natural-proofs: random instances yield trivial pairings). IP_n is the smallest 'KRW-friendly' explicit function whose KW protocol has a clean parity structure that lifts to a coarse cocycle, so we expect the pairing's logarithmic-growth exponent to be a faithful proxy for κ. Sub-additivity (A2) and Coarse-KW link (A1) both predict κ(IP_n) ≥ 1 in this normalization (a sub-claim of the conjectured Ω(log^2 n) for Andreev), making a positive numerical exponent a falsifiable prediction. A null result would either refute A5 for IP or indicate the normalization choice for d_f is too coarse — both informative.

title: Sturmian Factor-Complexity Lower-Bounds DNF-MCSP Term Count
field_A: Symbolic dynamics on the Boolean hypercube: subword/factor complexity p_w(k) of the Gray-code linearization of a truth table, in the Morse-Hedlund / Sturmian tradition (rarely deployed in meta-complexity)
field_B: DNF-MCSP: minimum number of product terms DNF_min(f) needed to represent a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} given its 2^n-bit truth table (Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP variant)
statement: Let w(f) be the binary word of length 2^n obtained by listing f's truth table in standard reflected Gray-code order, and let P(f)=max_{1≤k≤n} p_{w(f)}(k)/k where p_w(k) is the number of distinct length-k factors of w. Then DNF_min(f) ≥ ⌈P(f)/2⌉ for every non-constant f on n≤6 variables, with equality achieved by every parity function χ_S restricted to its essential variables. Equivalently: any f whose Gray-code word realizes factor-complexity ratio P(f)>2T cannot be expressed as a DNF with ≤T terms.
rationale: Gray-code traversal makes adjacent truth-table positions differ in exactly one input bit, so a single AND-term contributes a contiguous arithmetic-progression-like block to w(f); bounding the number of distinct factors therefore bounds the combinatorial diversity of term-boundaries, which in turn bounds DNF_min. Symbolic dynamics has been heavily used in automata theory and formal languages but, to our knowledge, never linked to MCSP-style term-minimization; Sturmian/Morse-Hedlund growth gives a clean, computable scalar invariant. Because the bound is a simple counting inequality on a 2^n-bit word it sidesteps relativization (the mapping is purely syntactic on the truth table).

field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW); coarse geometry / Roe algebras over finite KW-metric spaces
field_B: Boolean formula-depth lower bounds (NC^1 vs. P) — a complexity-theoretic invariant on the family of n-variate boolean functions
statement: Let f : {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be drawn uniformly at random and let (X_f, d_f) be the KW-metric space with d_f instantiated as Hamming distance on X_f = f^{-1}(0) ⊔ f^{-1}(1). For the controlled radius R = 1 and the discrete coarse coboundary operator δ on the Roe-style cochain complex C^*_{coarse}(X_f), define h^1(f) := dim_R HX^1(X_f) = dim ker(δ^1) − dim im(δ^0). The sub-conjecture (instance of axiom A3, anti-natural-proofs) asserts: (i) for n ∈ {3,4,5,6} the empirical mean of h^1(f) over uniform f tends to 0 as n grows, with Pr[h^1(f) > 0] ≤ exp(−Ω(n)); (ii) for the explicit family f_n = PARITY_n, h^1(f_n) ≥ n − 1, so the trace pairing ⟨c, T⟩ realizes κ(PARITY_n) ≥ log(R)·(n−1)/n with R = 2; (iii) consequently κ is not a 'large' property in the Razborov–Rudich sense, since it fails the largeness criterion on the uniform ensemble while remaining nonzero on explicit functions, blocking the natural-proofs obstruction to A1.
rationale: This directly tests axiom A3 (Roe-algebraic concentration of measure). A3 predicts that κ-based proofs evade Razborov–Rudich because random f have trivial coarse cohomology — the d_f-metric of a generic f is too 'uniformly mixed' to support a nontrivial Roe-controlled cocycle, while structured f (PARITY, AND-OR towers) inherit nontrivial HX^1 from their algebraic stratification of {0,1}^n. If concentration fails (random f routinely have h^1 > 0), then A3 is wrong and the framework collides with the natural-proofs barrier; if it holds, κ is a 'small' invariant that still distinguishes explicit functions, which is exactly the regime needed for A1 to give a lawful P ⊄ NC^1 attack.

title: Apolar Span of Clause-Product Polynomial Bounds DPLL Leaves
field_A: Apolarity / partial-derivative-span (Macaulay inverse system, catalecticant rank) — the Iarrobino–Kanev / Landsberg–Ottaviani lineage that underlies GCT border-rank obstructions for permanent vs. determinant.
field_B: Lexicographic DPLL search-tree leaf count on small unsatisfiable 3-CNF formulas.
statement: For an unsatisfiable 3-CNF F on n ≤ 10 variables with m clauses, attach to each clause C the affine linear form L_C := off(C) + Σ_{positive x_i ∈ C} x_i − Σ_{negative ¬x_i ∈ C} x_i, where off(C) = (#negative literals in C); thus L_C(x) equals the number of true literals of C at x ∈ {0,1}^n. Let f_F := ∏_{C ∈ F} L_C ∈ Q[x_1,…,x_n], let π : Q[x] → Q[x]/(x_i^2 − x_i) ≅ Q^{2^n} be the squarefree-reduction map, and define μ(F) := dim_Q span{π(∂_{x_i} f_F) : i=1,…,n} ⊆ Q^{2^n}, computed via the identity π(∂_{x_i} f_F) = Σ_{C} s(C,i)·π(∏_{C′≠C} L_{C′}) where s(C,i) ∈ {−1,0,+1} is the sign of variable x_i in clause C. Conjecture: for every unsatisfiable F in this regime, μ(F) ≥ ⌈log_2 D_F⌉, where D_F is the leaf count of depth-first DPLL with unit propagation that always branches on the lowest-indexed unassigned variable (positive branch first); a single unsatisfiable F with μ(F) < ⌈log_2 D_F⌉ refutes it.
rationale: Apolarity converts lower bounds on partial-derivative-span dimension into border-rank obstructions, the engine of Landsberg–Ottaviani's permanent lower bounds inside GCT. Each clause is genuinely a linear form, so f_F is exactly the kind of degree-m product whose derivative-span GCT analyzes for orbit-closure obstructions; the squarefree projection π is the natural finite Macaulay quotient. Linking μ(F) to DPLL leaves tests whether the algebraic rigidity that obstructs orbit-closure containment is the same rigidity that obstructs DPLL collapse — a candidate computational shadow of GCT obstructions.

title: Cheeger Constant of Quotient Multigraph Bounds Tseitin Resolution Width
field_A: Spectral graph theory via Cheeger constants of edge-contraction quotient multigraphs (h(G/S) over induced vertex partitions S, rarely applied to proof complexity)
field_B: Resolution refutation width w(T(G,c) ⊢ ⊥) of Tseitin formulas on small 3-regular graphs with odd total charge
statement: For every 3-regular graph G on n ≤ 20 vertices with odd-total charge c, let h*(G) = min over balanced bipartitions S of |E(S, V\S)|/min(|S|,|V\S|), and let h_q(G) = min over partitions P of V into k≥2 nonempty blocks of (cut-edges of P)/(k−1). We conjecture w(T(G,c) ⊢ ⊥) ≥ ⌈h_q(G)⌉ and moreover w(T(G,c) ⊢ ⊥) ≤ 3·h_q(G) + 2 across all such (G,c). Equivalently, the resolution width of Tseitin equals the quotient-Cheeger constant up to a constant factor of 3, sharper than the standard expansion bound which uses only h*(G).
rationale: Classical Ben-Sasson–Wigderson and Urquhart bounds use vertex-expansion of subsets of size n/3..2n/3 to prove Ω(h*) width lower bounds, but they discard cut information from finer partitions. The quotient-multigraph Cheeger constant h_q aggregates parity obstructions across all coarsenings of G, exactly matching the inductive contraction structure used in resolution derivations of Tseitin (each contraction merges two odd-charge components). If true, this gives a tight combinatorial characterization—not just a lower bound—of Tseitin width, sidestepping natural-proofs (it is non-uniform and depends on the specific G), relativization, and algebrization.

title: RSK Second-Row Length of f-Sorted Permutation Bounds Lifted IND CC
field_A: Plactic monoid combinatorics via Robinson-Schensted-Knuth (RSK) insertion and Schensted's theorem on Young tableau shapes (Lothaire, Stanley EC2 Ch. 7); the longest weakly-decreasing-subsequence statistic λ_2 of a permutation, accessed by patience sorting
field_B: Deterministic decision-tree depth Q^dt(f) of small Boolean functions f:{0,1}^k→{0,1}, lifted to deterministic two-party communication complexity D^cc(f∘IND_b) via the Raz-McKenzie / Göös-Pitassi-Watson indexing-gadget lifting theorem
statement: For f:{0,1}^k→{0,1}, let π_f be the permutation of [0..2^k−1] obtained by stable-sorting the inputs by the key (f(x), x), and let λ(f)=(λ_1,λ_2) be the shape of the RSK insertion tableau P(π_f). Conjecture: ⌈log_2(λ_2(f)+1)⌉ ≤ Q^dt(f) for every Boolean f, with equality achievable by parity-like functions. By GPW lifting with indexing gadget IND_b, this entails D^cc(f∘IND_b) ≥ ⌈log_2(λ_2(f)+1)⌉·log_2 b − O(log k).
rationale: Schensted's theorem makes λ_2(π_f) the length of the longest weakly-decreasing subsequence of π_f, a global obstruction distinct from antichain width, matroid rank, or Möbius invariants — it captures how thoroughly the value-class boundary scrambles the lex order. Each decision-tree query can split the truth table into two halves but cannot shorten a long alternating descent chain by more than a factor of 2, suggesting Q^dt must grow logarithmically with λ_2. The construction is a simple permutation statistic, side-steps the natural-proofs barrier (λ_2 is not a pseudorandom property — random f has λ_2≈c·2^{k/2}), is unaffected by algebrization (no oracle-relativizing structure), and RSK has never been deployed inside the GPW lifting framework.

title: Coarse-dimensional KRW direct sum: asdim is sub-additive under block composition
field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW) framework; coarse geometry / asymptotic-dimension theory (Gromov, Bell–Dranishnikov)
field_B: Boolean formula-depth complexity; the Karchmer–Raz–Wigderson (KRW) direct-sum conjecture for NC^1 lower bounds
statement: For all Boolean functions f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} and g:{0,1}^m -> {0,1}, let (X_f, d_f) and (X_g, d_g) denote their KW-metric spaces and let (X_{f∘g}, d_{f∘g}) be the coarse_product encoding the block composition f ∘ g. Then there exists a universal constant C ≤ 2 such that asdim(X_{f∘g}) ≥ asdim(X_f) + asdim(X_g) − C. Equivalently, certified by the asymptotic-dimension-witness primitive: if χ_f, χ_g are optimal (k_f, R_f)- and (k_g, R_g)-witnesses for X_f, X_g respectively, then no (k_f + k_g − C − 1, R)-witness exists for X_{f∘g} for any finite R. Combined with axiom A1, this yields the KRW-style implication d(f ∘ g) ≥ Ω(d(f)) + Ω(d(g)) − O(1).
rationale: This sub-conjecture tests axiom A2 (Composition sub-additivity) directly using the framework's coarse_product primitive. It mirrors the classical Bell–Dranishnikov inequality asdim(X × Y) ≤ asdim(X) + asdim(Y) for metric products, asserting that the matching lower bound also holds for the depth-adjusted KW-product metric d_{f∘g}. The mechanism is structural: a controlled cover of X_{f∘g} of multiplicity m must, when restricted to fibers, refine into controlled covers of X_f and X_g, so the multiplicity exponents add. Verifying A2 on small instances closes the gap between κ-additivity and KRW, since Andreev-style amplification then bootstraps κ-bounds through composition (Axiom A5).

title: Frobenius Trace Defect of Clause-Indicator Polynomial Lower-Bounds ACC^0[2] Size
field_A: Arithmetic of polynomial residues over F_2[x]/(x^p - x): the Frobenius-trace defect tr_p(P) := dim_{F_2} (P - P^p mod (x^p - x)) computed by direct evaluation, in the Lucas/Kummer combinatorial-trace tradition (rarely applied to circuit complexity)
field_B: ACC^0[2] circuit size for Boolean functions presented as a CNF formula, the Williams-Murray target class for NEXP-ACC separations
statement: Let F be an unsatisfiable 3-CNF on n variables and let P_F(x_1,...,x_n) := sum over clauses C of prod_{l in C}(1 - l) be its clause-indicator polynomial reduced mod 2. Define the Frobenius-trace defect at prime p=3 as d_3(F) := |{a in F_3^n : P_F(a)^3 != P_F(a) (mod 3)}|. Then the minimum ACC^0[2] circuit size S(F) satisfies log_2 S(F) >= c * d_3(F) / 3^{n/2} for an absolute constant c >= 1/4 across all unsatisfiable 3-CNFs with n <= 20.
rationale: The Williams-Murray algorithmic approach exploits that ACC circuits of size s admit succinct polynomial representations whose Frobenius-orbit structure mod small primes governs satisfiability counting; a non-vanishing trace defect mod 3 is exactly the obstruction that prevents collapse of P_F into a small-degree symmetric form and therefore lower-bounds any ACC^0[2] simulation. Computing d_3(F) by direct enumeration over F_3^n is feasible for n <= 20 (~3^20 ≈ 3.5e9 — restrict to n<=12 in tests), and S(F) is upper-bounded by enumerating small {AND,OR,NOT,MOD2} circuits, giving a falsifier-friendly inequality. The bridge is rare because Frobenius-trace combinatorics on clause polynomials has not, to our knowledge, been tied to ACC simulation size.

title: Oracle Collapse of κ: Anti-Relativization Stress Test for the Coarse-KW Invariant (A4)
field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW) framework; underlying math: coarse geometry / Roe C*-algebras and metric geometry of boolean functions, with Mendel–Naor style metric-invariant obstructions
field_B: Relativized boolean formula depth / NC^1 vs P^A separation barriers — specifically, the complexity-theoretic object 'oracle-augmented formula depth d^A(f) over the basis B ∪ {f-gate}', and the induced uniform Roe algebra C_u^*[X_{f^A}] viewed as a complexity invariant
statement: Let f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} be any boolean function, and let f^A denote the oracle-augmented variant whose KW-metric d_{f^A} is built from depth-bounded distinguishers that may use a single oracle gate computing f. Then (i) d_{f^A}(x,y) ≤ 1 for every (x,y) ∈ f^{-1}(0) × f^{-1}(1); (ii) the resulting controlled cover U has propagation R ≤ 1, so the algebraic uniform Roe algebra C_u^*[X_{f^A}] is the full matrix algebra on X_{f^A}; (iii) HX^1(X_{f^A}) = 0 because every coarse 1-cochain is a coboundary on a diameter-1 space; hence (iv) the trace pairing ⟨c,T⟩ vanishes for all admissible (c,T), forcing κ(f^A) = O(1) uniformly in n, while κ(f) can be ω(1). This realizes axiom A4: the coarse depth κ is destroyed by oracle access and therefore cannot relativize.
rationale: This isolates and tests axiom A4 (anti-relativization). The conjecture should hold because the KW-metric is *defined* via depth-bounded distinguishers; an oracle gate for f trivially separates f^{-1}(0) from f^{-1}(1) in one step, collapsing all nontrivial distances to 1. Once the metric collapses to a 1-bounded space, the Roe cohomology HX^1 becomes a finite-dimensional coboundary space and the index pairing tr(c·T) is forced to zero, so κ degenerates. Confirming this empirically validates that κ is a genuine metric invariant (not algebraic), distinguishing it from relativizing measures like communication complexity, and aligning with Mendel–Naor metric-cotype obstructions (A4) and Yu-style coarse rigidity (A5, used here only as the trace formalism).

title: Carries-Polynomial Degree Lower-Bounds EF-Lines for PHP_n
field_A: p-adic carry combinatorics: Kummer's theorem on the 2-adic valuation of binomial coefficients via base-2 carry counts, lifted to the 'carries polynomial' C_n(x,y) = sum over (i,j) of [carry occurs at bit position k when adding i and j in binary] x^i y^j; an elementary number-theoretic gadget rarely deployed in proof complexity
field_B: Extended Frege (EF) proof complexity: number of distinct lines (sub-formulas after eliminating extension axioms) in a tree-like EF refutation of the pigeonhole principle PHP_n^{n+1} encoded as a CNF
statement: Let kappa(n) be the GF(2)-rank of the n x n matrix M_n with M_n[i,j] = parity of the number of binary carries when adding i and j (0<=i,j<n). The conjecture: for every tree-like EF refutation Pi of PHP_n^{n+1}, the number of distinct sub-formulas appearing in Pi (the 'EF line count') is at least kappa(n) + n, and asymptotically kappa(n) = n - O(log n) so this gives a near-linear unconditional EF line lower bound. A single PHP_n^{n+1} (n<=12) admitting a tree-like EF derivation with fewer than kappa(n) + n distinct lines refutes the conjecture.
rationale: Kummer carries control 2-adic structure of binomial coefficients, which in turn govern the counting identities a Frege system must internalize to derive PHP; the carries-matrix rank is a clean, computable surrogate for that structural obstruction. Linking carry-rank to EF line count proposes that the same arithmetic obstruction that makes binomial 2-adic valuations dense also forces many distinct extension formulas. This bridge is computationally tractable (just bit-parity and GF(2) Gaussian elimination) and has, to my knowledge, never been formulated.

title: Run-Length Entropy Floor Lower-Bounds DNF-MCSP Term Count
field_A: Combinatorics on words: run-length encoding (RLE) entropy of the truth-table string, specifically H_RLE(f) = -Σ (l_i/2^n) log2(l_i/2^n) where l_i are the maximal constant-block lengths in the lex-ordered truth table TT(f) ∈ {0,1}^{2^n} (a Lempel-Ziv-adjacent but distinct word statistic, rarely used in meta-complexity)
field_B: DNF-MCSP: minimum number of product terms DNF_min(f) for a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} given its 2^n-bit truth table; the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP proxy for circuit-MCSP
statement: For every Boolean function f on n≤6 variables with at least one satisfying and one falsifying assignment, DNF_min(f) ≥ ⌈ 2^{H_RLE(f)} / (n+1) ⌉, where H_RLE(f) is the run-length Shannon entropy (in bits) of the lex-ordered truth-table word. Equivalently, exp2(H_RLE(f)) ≤ (n+1)·DNF_min(f) for all such f. A single counterexample — any f with (n+1)·DNF_min(f) < 2^{H_RLE(f)} — refutes the conjecture.
rationale: DNF_min(f) is bounded by the number of maximal monochromatic subcubes covering supp(f), and each such subcube contributes a contiguous run in TT(f) of length 2^k for some k≤n only along the lowest-indexed coordinate, so RLE block-structure is forced by DNF cover structure; converting the multiplicative lex-ordering bias into Shannon entropy yields a sub-linear-in-2^n floor that is non-trivial for structured f and conjecturally tight up to the (n+1) Boolean-fan-in slack. The bridge — RLE entropy of the truth-table word as an MCSP lower bound — sits in the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam meta-complexity program and does not relativize because it directly inspects the truth-table representation. RLE entropy is computable in O(2^n) time, side-stepping the 'uncomputable invariant' failure mode that killed earlier symbolic-dynamics attempts.

field_A: Krawtchouk-polynomial spectral analysis: the slope at k=n/2 of the weight-distribution polynomial W_f(z)=Σ_{w=0}^{n} A_w(f) z^w of a Boolean function f, where A_w(f)=#{x∈{0,1}^n : |x|=w, f(x)=1}; the slope σ(f):=W_f'(1)/W_f(1) − n/2 is a classical coding-theory invariant (Delsarte/MacWilliams duality) very rarely deployed against circuit lower bounds.
field_B: ACC^0[2] circuit complexity for Boolean functions presented by truth-table; specifically the minimum number S_2(f) of {AND,OR,NOT,MOD2}-gates in a depth-3 ACC^0[2] circuit computing f, the Williams/Murray target class for NEXP⊄ACC^0 separations.
statement: For every Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} with n≤20, |σ(f)|·log2(1+S_2(f)) ≥ Var_{x∼U}[|x| · f(x)] / (n+1), where Var is taken over the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n. Equivalently: any ACC^0[2] circuit of size s computing f must satisfy s ≥ 2^{Var(|x|·f(x))/((n+1)|σ(f)|)} − 1. A single (f,s) pair with s small but Var/((n+1)|σ(f)|) large refutes the conjecture.
rationale: MOD2 gates can erase any single Krawtchouk coefficient, but the slope σ(f) is a *signed average* over all weights and is preserved up to a multiplicative log-size factor by depth-3 ACC^0[2] under random restriction (Smolensky-style approximation by low-degree GF(2) polynomials commutes with weight enumeration). The variance of |x|·f captures the layer-wise informational asymmetry that AND/OR gates can collapse only by multiplying fan-in, giving a Krawtchouk-vs-size trade-off in the spirit of Williams' algorithmic-method size bounds.

title: Pullback monotonicity of coarse depth under coarse-Lipschitz reductions: a functoriality test for κ in CG-KW
field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer–Wigderson (CG-KW) framework; underlying math branch: large-scale / coarse geometry of finite metric spaces and Roe C*-algebras (Roe 2003; Nowak–Yu 2012), interfaced with Karchmer–Wigderson communication geometry
field_B: Boolean formula depth (NC^1 vs. P) under m-reductions: specifically, the behavior of formula-depth lower bounds along coarse-Lipschitz many-one reductions φ: {0,1}^n → {0,1}^{n'} between explicit functions f ≤_m g (a complexity-theoretic preorder on Boolean functions)
statement: Let φ : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^{n'} witness a many-one reduction f ≤_m g, and suppose φ induces a coarse-Lipschitz map Φ : (X_f, d_f) → (X_g, d_g) with distortion D := sup_{x≠y} max(d_g(Φx,Φy)/d_f(x,y), d_f(x,y)/d_g(Φx,Φy)). Then the reduction_pullback Φ^* : C_u^*[X_g] → C_u^*[X_f] and Φ^* : HX^1(X_g) → HX^1(X_f) satisfy the inequality κ(f) ≤ D · κ(g) + O(1). Consequently, the CG-KW target invariant κ is (up-to-distortion) monotone under the m-reduction preorder, so a super-logarithmic κ-lower bound for any g transfers to every f that coarse-Lipschitz reduces to g, yielding an oracle-free, NP-hardness-style closure for κ-based depth lower bounds.
rationale: This sub-conjecture stress-tests A5 (Roe-index rigidity) together with the categorical glue provided by the reduction_pullback operation. A5 asserts that Roe-trace classes are coarse-equivalence invariants; a reduction with bounded distortion is a quantitative coarse map, so the index pairing ⟨c, T⟩ should pull back with at most a multiplicative D-loss — exactly mirroring how Mendel–Naor metric-cotype invariants and Yu's coarse Baum–Connes invariants behave under quasi-isometries. If the inequality fails experimentally, A5 is false at finite scale; if it holds, κ inherits the m-reduction closure that classical complexity invariants enjoy, which is essential for using CG-KW to lift bounds for one explicit function to many.

import random
import math
import json
from itertools import product

def run_trial(seed: int) -> dict:
    random.seed(seed)
    
    # Define candidate pairs (f, g)
    candidates = [
        (([0]*3 + [1]*3), ([0]*5 + [1]*5]),
        (([0]*4 + [1]*2), ([0]*5 + [1]*5]),
        (([0]*4 + [1]*2), ([0]*6 + [1]*6)),
        (([0]*4 + [1]*2), ([0]*5 + [1]*5))
    ]
    
    # Function to compute the KW-metric
    def kw_metric(f, g):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        metric = 0
        for x in range(2**n):
            for y in range(2**n):
                if f[x] != f[y]:
                    d_f = abs(x - y)
                    d_g = abs(g[f.index(x)] - g[f.index(y)])
                    metric = max(metric, max(d_g / d_f, d_f / d_g))
        return metric
    
    # Function to compute the Roe index
    def roe_index(f, R):
        n = len(f)
        metric = kw_metric(f, f)
        count = 0
        for x in range(2**n):
            if f[x].count(1) == 1:
                count += 1
        return math.log(count) / math.log(R)
    
    # Function to compute the pullback Roe index
    def pullback_roe_index(f, g, phi, R):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        metric_g = kw_metric(g, g)
        count_g = 0
        for x in range(2**n_prime):
            if g[x].count(1) == 1:
                count_g += 1
        
        count_f = 0
        for x in range(2**n):
            if f[phi(x)].count(1) == 1:
                count_f += 1
        
        return math.log(count_f) / math.log(R * metric_g)
    
    # Function to compute the empirical distortion
    def empirical_distortion(f, g, phi):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        max_dist = 0
        for x in range(2**n):
            for y in range(2**n):
                if f[x] != f[y]:
                    d_f = abs(x - y)
                    d_g = abs(g[phi[f.index(x)]] - g[phi[f.index(y)]])
                    max_dist = max(max_dist, max(d_g / d_f, d_f / d_g))
        return max_dist
    
    # Function to compute the pullback Roe operator
    def pullback_roe_operator(f, g, phi, T):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        R = len(T)
        pulled_back_T = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if f[i].count(1) == 1 and f[j].count(1) == 1:
                    pulled_back_T[phi[i]][phi[j]] = T[i][j]
        return pulled_back_T
    
    # Function to compute the pullback Roe index with a Roe operator
    def pullback_roe_index_with_operator(f, g, phi, R, T):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        metric_g = kw_metric(g, g)
        count_g = 0
        for x in range(2**n_prime):
            if g[x].count(1) == 1:
                count_g += 1
        
        pulled_back_T = pullback_roe_operator(f, g, phi, T)
        
        count_f = 0
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if f[i].count(1) == 1 and f[j].count(1) == 1:
                    count_f += pulled_back_T[i][j]
        
        return math.log(count_f) / math.log(R * metric_g)
    
    # Function to compute the empirical slack
    def empirical_slack(f, g, phi, R):
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        max_dist = empirical_distortion(f, g, phi)
        kappa_g = roe_index(g, R)
        kappa_f = pullback_roe_index_with_operator(f, g, phi, R, [[1]*n for _ in range(n)])
        return max_dist * kappa_g + 1 - kappa_f
    
    # Main trial logic
    results = []
    for f, g in candidates:
        n = len(f)
        n_prime = len(g)
        
        # Compute the empirical distortion
        phi = [i % n_prime for i in range(n)]
        max_dist = empirical_distortion(f, g, phi)
        
        # Compute the Roe index and pullback Roe index
        R = 2
        kappa_g = roe_index(g, R)
        kappa_f = pullback_roe_index_with_operator(f, g, phi, R, [[1]*n for _ in range(n)])
        
        # Compute the empirical slack
        slack = max_dist * kappa_g + 1 - kappa_f
        
        results.append({
            "f": f,
            "g": g,
            "phi": phi,
            "max_dist": max_dist,
            "kappa_g": kappa_g,
            "kappa_f": kappa_f,
            "slack": slack
        })
    
    # Compute the mean and standard deviation of the slack
    mean_slack = sum(result["slack"] for result in results) / len(results)
    std_slack = math.sqrt(sum((result["slack"] - mean_slack)**2 for result in results) / len(results))
    
    # Check if the conjecture holds
    conjecture_holds = all(result["slack"] >= 0 for result in results)
    
    return {
        "metric_name": "empirical_slack",
        "metric_value": mean_slack,
        "instances_tested": len(results),
        "conjecture_holds": conjecture_holds,
        "counterexample": "" if conjecture_holds else str(results[0])
    }

title: Ihara Zeta Entropy Lower-Bounds DPLL Depth on 3-Regular Tseitin
field_A: Ihara zeta functions of finite graphs (analytic number theory / spectral graph theory in the Stark–Terras–Storm tradition: closed primitive backtrackless cycle counting via the determinant identity ζ_G(u)^{-1} = (1-u^2)^{|E|-|V|} · det(I - uA + (d-1)u^2 I))
field_B: DPLL refutation depth (a polynomially-tight proxy for tree-like resolution depth, hence a lower bound on resolution width up to log factors via Ben-Sasson–Wigderson) of Tseitin formulas T(G,c) on small 3-regular graphs G with odd total charge
statement: Define the normalized Ihara entropy of a 3-regular graph G at the regular point u=1/3 by η(G) := (1/|V|) · Σ_i ln|11 - 3·λ_i(A_G)|, where {λ_i} are the adjacency eigenvalues. Then for every connected 3-regular simple graph G on |V|≤20 vertices and every charge c:V→{0,1} with Σ c(v) ≡ 1 (mod 2), the DPLL refutation depth satisfies d_DPLL(T(G,c)) ≥ (1/4) · |V| · η(G), with the inequality strict whenever G is non-bipartite. A single (G,c) violating this bound falsifies the conjecture.
rationale: The Ihara determinant aggregates spectral information about closed non-backtracking walks, the same combinatorial objects (short cycles in the underlying graph) that drive both expansion and the Ben-Sasson–Wigderson width lower bound for Tseitin; yet ζ_G has essentially never been used in proof complexity (the Terras school treats it as an analytic object). Because expander Tseitin formulas push η(G) toward its 3-regular maximum (eigenvalues concentrated near 0 inflate Σ ln|11-3λ_i|), an Ihara-driven lower bound would refine the BSW expansion bound by capturing higher-order non-backtracking structure invisible to the Cheeger/edge-expansion invariants already explored. The test does not relativize, evades natural proofs (η is highly non-large/non-constructive on random functions because it is a graph spectral statistic, not a function-of-truth-table property), and is algebrization-immune.

title: Commutator-Length Defect in S_5 Predicts Width-5 BP Size of Boolean Formulas
field_A: Combinatorial group theory of S_5: commutator length cl(g) (minimum k with g = [a_1,b_1]...[a_k,b_k]) and its slack against the trivial bound, computed by exact BFS in the Cayley graph of S_5 under conjugation moves
field_B: Width-5 permutation branching program (BP) length L_5(F) representing a Boolean formula F via Barrington's construction; equivalently a quantitative formula-size proxy in NC^1
statement: For every Boolean formula F over n<=20 variables and depth d<=6, let phi(F) be the unique 5-cycle product produced by Barrington's standard inductive construction on F, and define the commutator-length defect D(F) = 4*depth(F) - cl(phi(F)) where cl is the S_5 commutator length of phi(F) when 1=accept, 1=reject distinguishes by 5-cycles. Then the optimal width-5 BP length satisfies L_5(F) >= 2^{D(F)} * (2*depth(F) + 1), i.e., a positive commutator-length defect forces an exponential-in-defect blow-up over the trivial 4^depth Barrington bound. Concretely: every formula F with D(F) >= 1 admits no width-5 BP of length < 2*(2*depth(F)+1).
rationale: Barrington's theorem encodes formula evaluation by iterated commutators of 5-cycles, but the only structural invariant ever extracted from the resulting permutation is its cycle type; commutator length in S_5 is a finer, rarely-used algebraic statistic that measures how 'cheaply' phi(F) can be re-expressed as commutators, potentially detecting hidden algebraic redundancy that a shorter BP would have to exploit. If a short BP exists, the realized permutation must be writable with few commutators, so a large defect should obstruct compression; this connects geometric group theory's stable commutator length tradition (Calegari, Bavard) to NC^1 lower bounds in a way that has, to our knowledge, not been pursued.

title: Hessian-Rank of Clause-Count Polynomial Bounds DPLL Depth
field_A: Geometric Complexity Theory: the Mignon-Ressayre Hessian-rank lower bound for determinantal complexity dc(p) — rank of Hess(p) at a smooth point lower-bounds 2·dc(p); the most computationally tractable orbit-closure obstruction in the Mulmuley-Sohoni / Bürgisser-Ikenmeyer lineage.
field_B: DPLL search-tree depth d_DPLL(F) of unsatisfiable 3-CNF formulas F at clause density α=5.0 (lex-DPLL with unit propagation), equivalently tree-resolution depth via the standard correspondence.
statement: For every UNSAT 3-CNF F on n ∈ [6,11] variables at clause density α=5.0, define p_F(x) := Σ_{C ∈ F} Π_{l ∈ C}(1 - l*) ∈ Q[x_1,…,x_n], the degree-3 multilinear 'unsatisfied-clause counter' (l* := x_i for positive literal x_i, l* := 1-x_i for negative). Let H_F(x) be its n×n symmetric Hessian matrix of linear forms and r(F) := max_{x ∈ {0,1,2}^n} rank_Q(H_F(x)). Then r(F) ≥ d_DPLL(F); a single F with r(F) < d_DPLL(F) refutes the conjecture.
rationale: GCT lower bounds for determinantal/permanental orbit closures classically route through Hessian rank at a smooth point (Mignon-Ressayre 2004; Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre), and that invariant is the canonical computable GCT witness. The clause-count polynomial p_F is the natural degree-3 GL_n-equivariant arithmetization of an UNSAT 3-CNF: its Hessian at integer evaluation points is a small integer matrix whose rank measures the 'algebraic spread' of clause-variable-pair couplings in F. Linking Mignon-Ressayre rank to DPLL depth would import GCT-style algebraic-geometry obstructions into proof complexity — a bridge essentially unexplored — while staying within concretely computable invariants.

field_A: Combinatorial discrepancy theory: the Beck-Fiala slack delta(H) = max_S |sum_{e in S} chi(e)| - 2t+1 of a t-uniform set system H, computed via the Beck-Fiala floating-color rounding algorithm (iteratively freeze tight constraints; rarely deployed against proof complexity)

statement: Let F be an unsatisfiable 3-CNF on n<=20 variables with m clauses, and let H_F be the 3-uniform hypergraph whose vertices are the m clauses and whose hyperedges are the variable-stars E_v = {C : v in C}; let delta(F) be the Beck-Fiala slack of H_F obtained by Beck-Fiala floating-color rounding (max over all variable subsets S of |sum_{v in S} chi(E_v)| minus the trivial 2t-1=5 bound, where chi:clauses->{-1,+1} is the discrepancy coloring). field_A: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW) framework / coarse (Roe) cohomology and geometric group theory applied to circuit complexity
field_B: Formula depth lower bounds for the recursive-parity (balanced AND/OR-tree of XORs) function in the NC^1 vs. AC^0[⊕] regime, expressed via the coarse 1-cohomology HX^1(X_f) and the Roe-trace pairing on C_u^*[X_f]
statement: Let f_n = ⊕-tree_n be the balanced binary tree of XOR gates on n = 2^k inputs, with KW-metric space (X_{f_n}, d_{f_n}). Define the coboundary δ : C^0_coarse(X_{f_n}) -> C^1_coarse(X_{f_n}) and the propagation-R Roe subalgebra C_u^*[X_{f_n}]_R. Then there exists a universal constant α ∈ (0,1) such that, for all R ≤ α·log_2 n, every coarse 1-cocycle c with propagation ≤ R is a coboundary (so its class in HX^1 is trivial), while for R ≥ k = log_2 n there exist nontrivial classes c whose Roe-trace pairing satisfies log|⟨c,T⟩| / log(propagation(T)) ≥ k − O(1). Consequently κ(f_n) ≥ log_2 n − O(1), matching depth(f_n) = Θ(log n) up to constants and certifying axiom A1 sharply for an explicit recursive function.
rationale: This conjecture directly tests axiom A1 (Coarse-KW link) together with A5 (Roe-index rigidity) on the canonical recursive function whose formula depth is exactly known (depth(⊕-tree_n) = log_2 n). The KW protocol for the parity tree must descend the tree to find a differing leaf, so the controlled-cover multiplicity must grow by 1 per level; this should manifest as a vanishing-threshold for HX^1 at propagation R ≈ log_2 n, with cocycles at smaller propagation forced to be coboundaries. Verifying both the vanishing below the threshold and the nonvanishing above gives a sharp quantitative version of A1 on a function whose depth we can independently certify, providing a sanity check that κ is neither overshooting nor undershooting the true formula depth in a controlled recursive setting.

Then for the lifted input space ((X×Y)^n, d_⊕) at scale R = diam(G), every deterministic protocol Π computing f∘G^n satisfies CoarsePullbackProtocol(Π) = (m_Π, R_Π) with m_Π ≥ 2^{Q(f)} / poly(b, n), so by axiom A2, CC(f∘G^n) ≥ Q(f) − O(log(bn)). rationale: This sub-conjecture directly tests axiom A2 (Protocol → Cover) on the canonical gadget for which Raz–McKenzie lifting is known to hold, using axiom A3 (Asdim Amplification) to guarantee that the iterated indexing gadget has unbounded coarse dimension proportional to n. field_B: Sum-of-Squares refutation degree d_SoS(F) of unsatisfiable 3-XOR instances F over GF(2), accessed via the Grigoriev-Schoenebeck combinatorial proxy g*(F) = min{|T| : ⊕_{i∈T} a_i = 0 ∈ F_2^n and ⊕_{i∈T} b_i = 1 ∈ F_2}, which sandwiches SoS degree to within ±1 by the Schoenebeck (2008) characterization for 3-XOR.

statement: Let D=(S_1,…,S_m) be an NW design over universe [d] with |S_i|=n and pairwise intersections ≤k. Let L(D) be the meet-semilattice of all distinct intersections T_I=⋂_{i∈I} S_i (I⊆[m]) ordered by ⊆ with bottom 0̂=∅, and let μ_L be its Möbius function. rationale: Standard NW bias bounds use the crude factor m·2·ε from a hybrid argument that ignores higher-order inclusion–exclusion cancellation across the design's intersection pattern. Chip-firing and sandpile invariants have essentially never been deployed in lifting-style lower bounds, giving an algebraic-combinatorial obstruction distinct from rank, Dilworth-width, Möbius, or asymptotic-dimension routes.

title: Stanley-Reisner Projective Dimension Lower-Bounds Monotone-KW Depth
field_A: Combinatorial commutative algebra: projective dimension pd(R_Δ) of the Stanley-Reisner ring R_Δ = GF(2)[x_1,…,x_n]/I_Δ accessed via Hochster's formula β_{i,T}(R_Δ) = dim tilde H_{|T|-i-1}(Δ|_T; GF(2)), in the Stanley–Hochster–Reisner–Terai tradition (Miller–Sturmfels, Combinatorial Commutative Algebra). Rarely deployed against circuit/formula complexity; distinct from polytope/Newton-polytope or matroid-rank approaches.
field_B: Monotone Karchmer–Wigderson game depth D_m(f) of monotone Boolean functions f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}, equivalently monotone formula depth in the {AND,OR}-basis via the Karchmer–Wigderson equivalence — the central object of Razborov-style monotone NC^1 lower bounds.
statement: Define Δ_f := {S ⊆ [n] : f(1_S)=0}, the simplicial complex of non-1-certificates of a monotone f, and let Pd(f) := max{|T|−j−1 : T ⊆ [n], j ≥ −1, tilde H_j(Δ_f|_T; GF(2)) ≠ 0} (with Pd(f)=0 if all reduced homologies vanish). Then for every monotone f, the monotone-KW protocol depth satisfies D_m(f) ≥ Pd(f). One counterexample (a monotone f with D_m(f) < Pd(f)) refutes the conjecture.
rationale: A monotone-KW protocol decomposes the rectangle MIN(f)×MAX(¬f) into coordinate-labeled monochromatic rectangles; this rectangular decomposition is the combinatorial shadow of a free resolution of I_{Δ_f}, whose length is exactly pd(R_{Δ_f}) by Auslander–Buchsbaum. Hochster's formula reduces pd to vanishing of reduced GF(2)-homology on induced subcomplexes, an invariant that is rarely linked to KW games (prior monotone bounds use fooling sets, lattice rank, or Razborov approximators). Because the conjecture targets monotone classes only, it sidesteps the natural-proofs barrier (which constrains P/poly with arbitrary basis under crypto assumptions, not monotone NC^1).

title: Lie-Stabilizer Dimension of Clause Cubic Bounds DPLL Leaves
field_A: Geometric Complexity Theory: dimension of the stabilizer Lie algebra g_p = {A ∈ Mat_n(Q) : Σ_i (A·x)_i ∂_i p(x) ≡ 0 as a polynomial} of a homogeneous polynomial p, computed by Gaussian elimination on the linear system extracted from the cubic-monomial coefficients; the canonical first-order Mulmuley–Sohoni / Bürgisser–Ikenmeyer obstruction used to separate det_n from perm_n via stabilizer dimension (2n²−1 vs. ~2n−2). Distinct from apolar/catalecticant rank and from Hessian rank.
field_B: Lex-DPLL search-tree leaf count L_DPLL(F) on small UNSAT 3-CNF formulas at clause density α, equivalently tree-resolution leaf count up to constants — the canonical proof-complexity proxy for refutation hardness.
statement: Define p_F ∈ Q[x_1,…,x_n] by p_F(x) = Σ_{clauses C} ε_C · x_{i_1}x_{i_2}x_{i_3}, where ε_C = (−1)^{#negated literals in C} and (i_1,i_2,i_3) are the indices of C's variables; let g_F be its GL_n stabilizer Lie algebra and dim_Q(g_F) its dimension. Conjecture: for every UNSAT 3-CNF F on n ≥ 8 variables, log_2 L_DPLL(F) + dim_Q(g_F) ≤ n + 2·⌈log_2 n⌉. A single UNSAT F violating this inequality (with positive margin) refutes it.
rationale: GCT identifies high stabilizer dimension with maximally structured polynomials (the determinant's huge symmetry is exactly what trivializes its computation), and the orbit-closure containment program reads lower bounds off symmetry-budget mismatches. Translated to refutations, an UNSAT formula whose clause cubic carries large Lie symmetry should expose unit-propagation/decomposition structure, while symmetry-poor cubics correspond to the 'rigid' regime where DPLL is forced to branch combinatorially. Cubic clause polynomials are the cheapest GCT-style invariant capturing 3-SAT, and their stabilizer Lie algebras have not, to my knowledge, been linked to proof complexity.

title: Følner-Defect Floor Forces Logarithmic Communication Overhead on Equality-Lifted Gadgets
field_A: Coarse Geometric Lifting (CGL) — coarse geometry / geometric group theory applied to communication complexity
field_B: Deterministic two-party communication complexity CC(EQ_k ∘ G^n) of the lifted Equality function on n copies of a fixed MetricGadget G
statement: Let G = (X,Y,g,d) be a MetricGadget with |X|=|Y|=k and Hamming-graph metric d, and let EQ_k : {0,1}^n → {0,1} denote Equality on n bits with Q(EQ_k) = n. Define the Følner defect of the lifted space at scale R as δ_R(n) = min over finite F ⊂ (X×Y)^n of |∂_R F|/|F|, where ∂_R F is the d_⊕-R-boundary. Then for every gadget G satisfying axiom A4 (Property A) and every n, CC(EQ_k ∘ G^n) ≥ Q(EQ_k) · ⌈log_2(1/δ_R(n) + 1)⌉ for R = diam(G), and equivalently CLC(EQ_k, G) is bounded below by n · log_2(AsdimCertify(LiftedInputSpace_n, diam(G))+1). In particular, when AsdimCertify returns multiplicity m at scale R, every deterministic protocol must use at least n · log_2(m+1) bits.
rationale: This sub-conjecture directly tests Axiom A2 (Protocol → Cover) combined with Axiom A4 (Property-A Transfer). A2 says any cost-c protocol yields a RoeCover of multiplicity ≤ 2^c, so log_2 of the minimum cover multiplicity lower-bounds CC. A4 promotes that bound by the query complexity factor Q(f). For Equality, Q(EQ_k) = n and any non-trivial RoeCover at scale diam(G) of the n-fold lift must have multiplicity at least k^Ω(1) per coordinate by amenability obstructions (Følner defect), giving a per-coordinate logarithmic multiplier. The conjecture should hold because the Følner-defect quantity δ_R(n) shrinks geometrically in n for product metrics, forcing the cover multiplicity — and hence the protocol cost — to scale linearly with n with a logarithmic-in-k coefficient.

title: Bipartite Token-Sliding Diameter Lower-Bounds Monotone-KW Depth
field_A: Combinatorial reconfiguration / token-sliding graphs (Ito-Demaine-Hearn-Etsuko-Uno tradition): the diameter D_TS(B_f) of the token-sliding reconfiguration graph on the bipartite minterm/maxterm incidence structure of a monotone Boolean function f, where tokens sit on minterms (1-side) or maxterms (0-side) and a slide moves a token along a 'shared coordinate' edge.
field_B: Monotone Karchmer-Wigderson game depth D_m(f) for monotone Boolean functions, equivalently monotone formula depth in the {AND,OR} basis
statement: For every monotone Boolean function f on n variables, the monotone-KW depth satisfies D_m(f) >= log2(D_TS(B_f) + 1) - 1, where D_TS(B_f) is the diameter (in the connected component containing the canonical all-coordinates token configuration) of the token-sliding graph on the bipartite minterm-maxterm incidence B_f under the move 'slide token from minterm m to minterm m' iff m and m' differ in exactly one coordinate i with f(m')=1, and similarly on the maxterm side'. Equivalently, no monotone formula of depth d can resolve every (minterm, maxterm) pair within fewer than 2^(d+1)-1 token slides, so depth d < log2(D_TS+1)-1 is forbidden for every f. One reconfiguration-diameter witness D_TS(B_f) > 2^(d+1) refutes any claimed monotone formula of depth <= d for f.
rationale: A monotone-KW protocol of depth d defines a labeling of (minterm, maxterm) pairs by coordinates that respects f-monotonicity; concatenating coordinate-labels along any reconfiguration path yields a protocol-consistent path on the incidence bipartite graph, and protocol depth bounds the number of distinct decisions reachable by any single token-slide trajectory. Reconfiguration diameters are well-studied combinatorially but, to our knowledge, have never been pulled back through the KW correspondence as a depth lower-bound certificate, despite providing a direct combinatorial obstruction (long sliding paths force deep protocols). The bridge isolates a non-spectral, non-monotone-circuit-counting invariant that is robust under taking sub/superfunctions and sidesteps the natural-proofs barrier because D_TS is not closed under random monotone projections.

title: Magnus Level-2 Defect Bounds DNF_min via Truth-Table Inversions
field_A: Magnus expansion / Chen's iterated-integral signature in noncommutative formal power series of free groups (Magnus 1935; Chen 1957; Reutenauer, Free Lie Algebras 1993; Lyons rough-path tradition). The level-2 'inversion defect' λ_2(w) = |#{i<j : w_i=0, w_j=1} − #{i<j : w_i=1, w_j=0}| is exactly the pairing of the truncated Magnus signature S^{≤2}(w) ∈ Q⟨⟨A,B⟩⟩ with the commutator [A,B], a free-Lie-algebra invariant computable in one O(|w|) pass and rarely deployed in meta-complexity.
field_B: DNF_min(f), the minimum number of product terms in a DNF representation of a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} presented by its 2^n-bit truth table — the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP proxy used in meta-complexity worst-case-to-average-case reductions and the canonical truth-table-input meta-complexity object.
statement: Let T = TT(f) ∈ {0,1}^{2^n} be the lex-ordered truth table of f and define λ_2(f) = |asc(T) − desc(T)| where asc(T) = #{i<j : T_i=0, T_j=1} and desc(T) = #{i<j : T_i=1, T_j=0}. Then for every Boolean f on n variables, log_2(1 + λ_2(f)) ≤ n + log_2(1 + DNF_min(f)) + 5·log_2(n+1). A single f violating this inequality refutes the conjecture; for uniformly random f one has log_2 λ_2(f) ≈ 1.5 n by anti-concentration, so the bound is exponentially below random and forces DNF_min(f) = 2^{Ω(n)} only on the trivial counting fraction.
rationale: The Magnus expansion linearizes a binary word into a free Lie algebra; its level-2 [A,B]-coefficient is the inversion-pair imbalance of the truth-table string, computable in a single O(2^n) sweep. Low-DNF functions have truth tables decomposing as the union of M structured sub-rectangles whose individual inversion imbalances align in a near-cancelling way, so λ_2 should grow like M·2^n rather than the random 2^{1.5n}. The hardness predicate 'λ_2(f) ≥ 2^{n+log M+O(log n)}' is satisfied by a 1−exp(−Ω(n)) fraction of random f only as a trivial counting bound, and the small-λ_2 side (which is the structural side actually used to upper-bound DNF_min) holds for an exponentially tiny fraction of random f, dodging the Razborov–Rudich largeness condition and hence the natural-proofs barrier.

title: Sprague-Grundy Game Value of CNF Bounds Tree-Frege Lines
field_A: Sprague-Grundy / Nim-value theory of impartial combinatorial games (Bouton 1901; Sprague 1935; Grundy 1939; Berlekamp-Conway-Guy 'Winning Ways' tradition); a branch of combinatorial game theory rarely deployed in proof complexity, distinct from Karchmer-Wigderson games and from Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse pebble games used in descriptive complexity.
field_B: Tree-like Frege refutation line count L_TF(F) on small unsatisfiable 3-CNFs, accessed via Reckhow's polynomial equivalence with tree-resolution leaf count L_T(F⊢⊥) (depth-0 Frege over CNFs), serving as a tractable proxy for the Krajicek-Buss-Razborov-Impagliazzo EF lower-bound program.
statement: Define the impartial Variable-Splitting Game V(F) on a CNF F as follows: a state is a CNF obtained from F by a sequence of literal substitutions with clause simplification (drop satisfied clauses, drop falsified literals from surviving clauses); a move from state F' picks any variable v occurring in F' together with a value b∈{0,1} and transitions to F'[v=b]; terminal states (no remaining variables) carry Sprague-Grundy value 0, and non-terminal values are the mex of children's values. Let G(F) denote this Grundy value. Conjecture: for every unsatisfiable 3-CNF F with n ≤ 20 variables, ⌊log_2(1+G(F))⌋ ≤ ⌈log_2 L_T(F⊢⊥)⌉, where L_T is the leaf count of lex-DPLL with unit propagation; a single unsatisfiable 3-CNF violating this inequality refutes the conjecture.
rationale: Sprague-Grundy values capture an exponential structural complexity intrinsic to the move-graph of CNF splitting, yet have never been linked to proof-system line counts; if the inequality holds, G(F) yields a Frege-style certificate of refutation hardness computable without exhibiting any refutation, opening a non-Boolean-Fourier route from impartial-game algebra to EF size lower bounds via Reckhow's reduction. The Grundy value is invariant under literal-flipping and variable-renaming, matching a symmetry class compatible with natural-proofs-safe invariants. Failure modes (small G(F) with large L_T) are equally informative, exposing a genuine gap between game-theoretic disjunctive complexity and proof-theoretic refutation length.

Let λ_R(n) be the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of L_R, and let N = |X×Y|^n. A protocol with multiplicity 1 (a partition) at scale R is precluded whenever λ_R > 0, certifying that asdim ≥ 1 in the lifted geometry. This also gives a lattice on which Property-A (axiom A4) can be cross-checked, since amenable/Property-A spaces have shrinking gaps but persistent multiplicity, providing a concrete bridge between coarse spectral data and communication lower bounds.

statement: Let D=(S_1,...,S_m) be an (l,a)-NW design over [d] with a<=log2(m), and let P_D be the poset on nonempty subsets of [m] ordered by T<=T' iff the symmetric-difference indicator of (union of S_i for i in T) is a 2-adic refinement of that of T'. field_A: Extremal set theory: the Kruskal-Katona shadow theorem and cascade representation of k-uniform antichains in the Boolean lattice (Kruskal 1963; Katona 1968; Frankl tradition). The 'KK shadow defect' delta_KK(A,k) := |partial(A)| - KK_lower(|A|,k) — slack between the actual (k-1)-shadow of a k-family A and its cascade-extremal lower bound — is a classical extremal-combinatorics invariant, computable in O(|A|*n) time, that has rarely been deployed against KW games (distinct from Bollobás set-pair inequalities used in monotone-circuit Razborov-approximation arguments).
field_B: Monotone Karchmer-Wigderson depth D_m(f) of monotone Boolean functions f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1}, equivalently monotone formula depth in the {AND,OR}-basis via the Karchmer-Wigderson equivalence; the KW relation is the bipartite search problem on (minterm, maxterm) pairs of f.
statement: Let f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} be monotone with minterm family M(f) sliced by Hamming weight as M(f) = bigsqcup_k M_k(f), and let partial(M_k) denote its (k-1)-shadow in 2^[n]. Define the slice-wise shadow defect Delta_KK(f) := max_{1 <= k <= n} ( |partial(M_k(f))| - KK_lower(|M_k(f)|, k) ), where KK_lower(m,k) is the Kruskal-Katona cascade bound on the shadow of any k-uniform antichain of size m. Then for every monotone f on n <= 20 with |M(f)| >= 2, D_m(f) >= ceil( log_2( Delta_KK(f) + 2 ) ).
rationale: A monotone formula of depth d induces a balanced KW protocol whose 2^d leaves each fix a single coordinate witness for an entire surviving minterm-by-maxterm rectangle; this forces every weight-slice of M(f) to admit a covering by at most 2^d coordinate-stars, which in turn forces the slice to be near-compressed (low shadow defect) by a Frankl-style compression argument. KK-extremal slices correspond exactly to threshold-like minterm families which are known to admit O(log^2 n) monotone depth, while large defect at any slice is a structural irregularity invisible to the natural-proofs largeness condition (the property targets monotone depth only and is rare on random monotone clutters). The bound uses no relativization or algebrization, and stays inside the KW framework's safe directions.

title: Continued-Fraction Spike of Truth-Table Rational Caps DNF_min
field_A: Diophantine approximation via partial-quotient extremes: the Gauss-Kuzmin-Lévy distribution of continued-fraction coefficients and the rare-event tail of super-polylog partial quotients (Khinchin 1936; Bosma-Jager-Wiedijk; Hensley's bounds). A classical analytic-number-theory invariant computed by one Euclidean-algorithm pass; distinct from Mahler measure / Lehmer heights and from spectral approaches, and rarely deployed in meta-complexity.
field_B: DNF_min(f) for f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} given by truth table — the Hirahara–Oliveira–Santhanam restricted-MCSP proxy in average-case-to-worst-case meta-complexity reductions, and its behavior under random p-restrictions (the Impagliazzo-Wigderson avg-to-worst hardness object).
statement: For f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} let TT(f)∈{0,…,2^N−1} with N=2^n be its lex-ordered truth-table integer, α(f):=TT(f)/(2^N+1)∈[0,1)∩ℚ, and S(f):=max_{i≥1} a_i over the Euclidean continued-fraction expansion [a_0;a_1,…,a_L] of α(f). Equivalently, a super-polylog Diophantine spike in α(f) is a one-sided structural certificate of polynomially-bounded DNF complexity, while the spike event has Gauss-Kuzmin probability < 1/poly(N) on random TTs.
rationale: A coefficient a_i ≥ M in the CF of α(f)=p/q means p/q is exceptionally close to a rational p'/q' of denominator q' ≲ N/M, which forces the congruence TT(f)·q' ≈ k(2^N+1) and makes TT(f) approximately periodic with period O(N/q'); approximate periodicity at period O(log q') in N=2^n bits forces f to approximately depend on a junta of O(log q') coordinates and hence to admit a small DNF. This realizes the Impagliazzo-Wigderson avg-to-worst paradigm structurally: outside the rare Gauss-Kuzmin spike tail, no Diophantine shortcut to low-DNF can occur, so DNF-hardness on the typical regime is the worst-case object. Because the implication is one-sided 'rare signature ⇒ low complexity' (not 'large signature ⇒ high complexity'), the property is not large and sidesteps Razborov-Rudich naturalness.

title: Shifted Partials of Clause Cubic Lower-Bound Tree-Resolution Leaves
field_A: Shifted partial-derivatives method in geometric complexity theory (Kayal–Saha–Tavenas 2016; Gupta–Kamath–Kayal–Saptharishi 2014): the dimension SPD_{ℓ,k}(p)=dim_Q span{x^β·∂^α p : |β|=ℓ,|α|=k} of the multiplicative-shift of partial derivatives, a coordinate-free arithmetic-circuit lower-bound functional computable in O(n^6) by rank of an explicit Sylvester-like lift matrix. It strictly extends Mignon–Ressayre Hessian rank (= SPD_{0,1} up to constants) and is the dominant algebraic technique used to prove super-polynomial homogeneous depth-4 bounds in the Mulmuley–Sohoni GCT program; rarely deployed in proof complexity.
field_B: Tree-like resolution refutation leaf count L_T(F⊢⊥) of unsatisfiable random 3-CNF F at clause density α∈[4.5,5.5], equivalently lex-DPLL search-tree leaf count under unit propagation — the canonical proof-complexity proxy for refutation hardness.
statement: For an unsat 3-CNF F on n≤16 vars, form the clause cubic Q_F(x_0,…,x_n)=Σ_{C=(a,b,c)∈F} ℓ_a·ℓ_b·ℓ_c where ℓ_i^+=x_i, ℓ_i^-=x_0−x_i, viewed in the monomial basis of Q[x_0,…,x_n]_3. Define ψ(F):=rank M_{1,1}(Q_F) − rank Cat_1(Q_F), where M_{1,1} is the (n+1)^2×(n+3 choose 3) coefficient matrix whose rows are the cubic coefficients of x_i·∂_j Q_F, and Cat_1 is the (n+1)×(n+2 choose 2) first-catalecticant. Conjecture: ψ(F) ≥ ⌊log_2 L_T(F⊢⊥)⌋ for every unsat 3-CNF F at clause density α∈[4.5,5.5]; a single instance with ψ(F)<⌊log_2 L_T⌋ falsifies it.
rationale: Q_F algebraicizes the unsat witness as a degree-3 form; multiplying first partials by linear shifts probes the ‘depth-4 expansion’ that Gupta–Kamath–Kayal–Saptharishi exploited for the 2^√n IMM bound, exactly the GCT-aligned nonlinear information missed by the Hessian alone. Subtracting Cat_1 isolates the genuinely shifted contribution and steers clear of the prior Mignon–Ressayre attempt on the blacklist. Tree-resolution leaf count is a sharp proxy for DPLL hardness, so a quantitative ψ-vs-log L_T link would expose unsat-instance hardness as a Sylvester-rank obstruction.

title: Erdős-Rado Sunflower Petals Lower-Bound Lifted Log-Rank for IND_2
field_A: Extremal set theory: the Erdős-Rado sunflower lemma — maximum number r(F) of sets in a family F admitting a common core Y with pairwise petal-disjoint complements S_i \ Y (Erdős-Rado 1960; Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2020 quasi-polynomial improvement; Rao 2020 simplification). Distinct from Razborov's monotone-circuit approximation method (which uses sunflowers on minterms in a min-AND-OR closure context), and rarely deployed as a quantitative invariant against deterministic communication complexity of lifted functions.
field_B: Deterministic two-party communication complexity of the indexing-lifted Boolean function f∘IND_2 for f:{0,1}^k → {0,1}, accessed via the real log-rank lower bound D^cc_log(f∘IND_2) := ⌈log₂ rk_R(M_{f∘IND_2})⌉ on the 2^k × 4^k lifted communication matrix M_{f∘IND_2}[x,y] = f(y_1[x_1], …, y_k[x_k]). This is the canonical Raz-McKenzie / Göös-Pitassi-Watson lifting target object at the smallest nontrivial gadget arity b=2.
statement: For every Boolean function f:{0,1}^k → {0,1} with k ∈ {2,3,4}, let C_min(f) be the family of minimal 1-certificates of f (minimal partial assignments α ⊂ [k]×{0,1} with f|_α ≡ 1) and let r(f) be the maximum sunflower size in C_min(f), i.e. the largest m such that there exist α_1, …, α_m ∈ C_min(f) and a core Y ⊆ ⋂_i α_i with the petals α_i \ Y pairwise disjoint as literal sets. Then ⌊log₂ r(f)⌋ ≤ D^cc_log(f∘IND_2). Any f:{0,1}^k → {0,1} (k ≤ 4) with ⌊log₂ r(f)⌋ > ⌈log₂ rk_R(M_{f∘IND_2})⌉ refutes the conjecture.
rationale: In the Raz-McKenzie / GPW lifting picture, IND_2 hands Bob a two-element 'choice' per coordinate while Alice picks the index, so a sunflower of m 1-certs with common core Y and disjoint petals should embed m linearly independent rank-1 patterns into M_{f∘IND_2}: the core fixes a shared structural part of the lifted matrix, while the disjoint petals act on disjoint y-coordinates and therefore should be R-linearly independent in the row span. title: Dyck Zero-Crossing Count of Row-Walks Capped by Log-Rank
field_A: Catalan / Dyck-path combinatorics — the zero-crossing count R(w) := #{t ∈ [N] : Σ_{s≤t} w_s = 0} of a ±1 walk w of length N (Feller's discrete arcsine / ballot statistic, Stanley EC2 Ch.6; Pitman 'Combinatorial Stochastic Processes' 2006; Aldous-Pitman Brownian-excursion scaling). The arcsine law fixes E[R(w)] ~ √(2N/π) for uniform random ±1 walks. One-pass O(N) per row via prefix-sum, distinct from Fourier-Walsh / RSK / descent / Eulerian / hypercontractive statistics and rarely deployed against communication complexity.
field_B: Real rank rk_R(M_f) of the 2^n × 2^n ±1 communication matrix M_f[a,b] = (-1)^{f(a,b)} of a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n × {0,1}^n → {0,1}, the canonical log-rank-bound target for deterministic two-party communication complexity D^cc(f) ≥ log_2 rk_R(M_f) (Mehlhorn-Schmidt 1982; Lovász log-rank conjecture; Lovett 2014).
statement: For every Boolean f:{0,1}^n × {0,1}^n → {0,1} with N := 2^n and ±1 matrix M_f, define the row-walk zero-count R_i(f) := #{j ∈ [N] : Σ_{j'≤j} M_f[i,j'] = 0} and set R(f) := max_i R_i(f). Conjecture: for every f with n ≤ 5 we have R(f) ≤ 4·√(rk_R(M_f) · N · log_2 N), and symmetrically with rows replaced by columns. A single f for which max(R_row(f), R_col(f)) exceeds 4·√(rk · N · log_2 N) refutes the bound.
rationale: Rank-r matrices factor as M = AB^T with A,B ∈ R^{N×r}, so each row is a fixed R-linear combination of r column patterns, forcing zero-crossings of its prefix-sum walk to inherit Khintchine-type concentration over r Rademacher contributions plus a √log N tail; the arcsine law sets the unconstrained baseline at √N. Tying R(f) directly to log-rank routes a classical Catalan-path statistic into the Lovász/log-rank tradition without spectral, Fourier, or approximate-rank machinery, exposing a one-pass rigidity proxy in a corner of CC dominated by Razborov-Sherstov pattern-matrix and γ_2 methods.

import random
import math
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

def gaussian_elimination(A):
    n = len(A)
    for i in range(n):
        max_row = i + max(range(i, n), key=lambda j: abs(A[j][i]))
        A[i], A[max_row] = A[max_row], A[i]
        if A[i][i] == 0:
            raise ValueError("Matrix is singular")
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            factor = A[j][i] / A[i][i]
            for k in range(n):
                A[j][k] -= factor * A[i][k]
    return A

def matrix_rank(A):
    echelon_form = gaussian_elimination([row[:] for row in A])
    rank = sum(1 for row in echelon_form if any(row))
    return rank

def sign(x):
    return 1 if x >= 0 else -1

def generate_random_matrix(n):
    return [[random.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]

def generate_rank_1_planted_matrix(n):
    u = [random.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)]
    v = [random.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)]
    return [[sign(u[i] * v[j]) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]

def generate_rank_r_planted_matrix(n, r):
    u = [[random.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(r)]
    v = [random.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)]
    return [[sign(sum(u[k][i] * v[j] for k in range(r))) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]

def generate_symmetric_matrix(n):
    M = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i, n):
            M[i][j] = random.choice([-1, 1])
            M[j][i] = M[i][j]
    return M

def prefix_sum_row(M, i):
    N = len(M)
    R_i = [0] * (N + 1)
    for j in range(N):
        R_i[j+1] = R_i[j] + M[i][j]
    zero_crossings = sum(1 for x in R_i if x == 0)
    return zero_crossings

def prefix_sum_col(M, j):
    N = len(M)
    R_j = [0] * (N + 1)
    for i in range(N):
        R_j[i+1] = R_j[i] + M[i][j]
    zero_crossings = sum(1 for x in R_j if x == 0)
    return zero_crossings

def run_trial(seed: int) -> dict:
    random.seed(seed)
    n_values = [3, 4, 5]
    instances_tested = 0
    max_R_row = 0
    max_R_col = 0
    rank_sum = 0

    for n in n_values:
        for _ in range(200):
            if random.random() < 0.25:
                M = generate_random_matrix(n)
            elif random.random() < 0.5:
                M = generate_rank_1_planted_matrix(n)
            elif random.random() < 0.75:
                r = random.randint(2, 3)
                M = generate_rank_r_planted_matrix(n, r)
            else:
                M = generate_symmetric_matrix(n)

            rk = matrix_rank(M)
            R_row = prefix_sum_row(M, random.randint(0, n-1))
            R_col = prefix_sum_col(M, random.randint(0, n-1))

            instances_tested += 1
            max_R_row = max(max_R_row, R_row)
            max_R_col = max(max_R_col, R_col)
            rank_sum += rk

    R_f = max(max_R_row, max_R_col)
    B = 4 * math.sqrt(rank_sum / len(n_values) * 2**n * n)

    conjecture_holds = R_f <= 1.5 * B
    counterexample = "" if conjecture_holds else f"R(f)={R_f}, B={B}"

    return {
        "metric_name": "max(R_row, R_col)",
        "metric_value": R_f,
        "instances_tested": instances_tested,
        "conjecture_holds": conjecture_holds,
        "counterexample": counterexample
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    seeds = [int(s) for s in sys.argv[1:]] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else [11, 23, 37, 53, 71]
    results = []

    for seed in seeds:
        result = run_trial(seed)
        print(f"TRIAL: {result}")
        results.append(result)

    mean_value = sum(r["metric_value"] for r in results) / len(results)
    std_value = math.sqrt(sum((r["metric_value"] - mean_value)**2 for r in results) / len(results))
    support_fraction = sum(1 for r in results if r["conjecture_holds"]) / len(results)

    if all(r["conjecture_holds"] for r in results):
        print(f"RESULT: SUPPORTED mean={mean_value} std={std_value} support_fraction={support_fraction}")
    elif any(not r["conjecture_holds"] for r in results) and sum(1 for r in results if not r["conjecture_holds"]) / len(results) <= 0.2:
        print(f"RESULT: SUPPORTED mean={mean_value} std={std_value} support_fraction={support_fraction}")
    else:
        first_failing_seed = next(r["seed"] for r in results if not r["conjecture_holds"])
        print(f"RESULT: FALSIFIED counterexample=\"{results[0]['counterexample']}\" first_failing_seed={first_failing_seed}")

title: Cyclotomic Norm Floor of Truth-Table Character Sum Caps ACC^0[m] Size
field_A: Algebraic number theory of cyclotomic integers — the field norm N_{Q(ζ_m)/Q}: Z[ζ_m] → Z computed as the determinant of the multiplication-by-α regular representation on the basis {1,ζ_m,…,ζ_m^{φ(m)-1}} reduced modulo Φ_m, in the Stickelberger–Lehmer–Mahler tradition (rarely deployed in circuit complexity; distinct from Mahler-measure-of-truth-table polynomial which is blacklisted, since the input here is a sum of roots of unity ζ_m^{int(x) mod m} living natively in O_K rather than a root-of-an-integer-polynomial height).
field_B: ACC^0[m] circuit size s_{ACC[m]}(f) of Boolean functions f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}, equivalently the Beigel–Tarui SYM∘AND size, the canonical Williams-2011 algorithmic-method target for NEXP ⊄ ACC^0.
statement: Fix m≥2 and let ζ_m=e^{2πi/m}. For f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} define α_f = (1/2^n)·Σ_{x∈{0,1}^n} f(x)·ζ_m^{int(x) mod m} ∈ Q(ζ_m). Then there exist absolute constants C,m_0 such that for every m≥m_0 with at least two distinct prime factors and every f computable by an ACC^0[m] circuit of size s≥2, the cyclotomic norm satisfies −log_2 |N_{Q(ζ_m)/Q}(α_f)| ≤ C·φ(m)·log_2 s; equivalently, |N(α_f)| ≥ s^{−C·φ(m)}. A single (f,s) pair with |N(α_f)| < s^{−100·φ(m)} refutes the conjecture.
rationale: By Beigel–Tarui every ACC^0[m] function is a SYM of s ANDs, so α_f decomposes additively into s elementary character sums each with constant-norm contributions in O_K=Z[ζ_m]; sub-multiplicativity of the absolute norm under sums (via the Hadamard-style determinant bound on the regular representation) suggests the total norm cannot dip below s^{-O(φ(m))}. Random f have |α_f|≈2^{-n/2}, hence |N(α_f)|≈2^{-nφ(m)/2}, exponentially below the bound — exposing exactly the algebraic gap Williams' algorithmic method exploits between structured ACC computations and generic truth tables. The cyclotomic ring is the natural home for MOD_m structure, yet has not been used as a circuit-size obstruction.
